purpose.title: What should this job do?

both.label: Back up and archive
both.hint: Restore folders, calendar, contacts and whole mailboxes, and keep every mail tamper-evident as well (recommended).

backup.label: Back up
backup.hint: Restore folders, calendar, contacts and whole mailboxes as they were at a restore point.

archive.label: Archive
archive.hint: Keep every mail tamper-evident, captured before users can change or delete it, for the GoBD, retention periods and legal hold.

capture.title: How mail reaches the archive: Exchange journaling
capture.journaling: Exchange sends a copy of every mail to {appName} while it is in transport, before it reaches the mailbox, so nobody can change or delete it first. Journaling is set up once per tenant: a journal address and a journal rule in Microsoft 365.

backupOnly.title: Backups alone keep no mail between two runs
backupOnly.description: A backup sees the mailbox as it is when it runs. Mail that arrives and is deleted before the next run is in no backup, and backups are not tamper-evident. Archiving captures every mail as it arrives.

purpose.archiveOnlySchedule: This job makes no backups on a schedule: mail is captured by the archive as it arrives. Calendar, contacts and folders are only backed up when someone starts the job.

rarer.title: Backups can run less often
rarer.description: The archive already captures every mail as it arrives, so backups only keep what journaling does not see: folders, calendar, contacts and read status. Every 8 hours is usually enough and puts less load on Microsoft 365. This is a suggestion; the schedule stays as you set it.

gap.hours: Mail that arrives and is deleted within the {count, plural, one {one hour} other {# hours}} between two backups is in no backup.
gap.minutes: Mail that arrives and is deleted within the {count, plural, one {one minute} other {# minutes}} between two backups is in no backup.
gap.between: Mail that arrives and is deleted between two backups is in no backup.

archive.noObjectLock: This tenant's storage has no Object Lock. The archive is then immutable at application level only: whoever can reach the storage or the server can change or delete data.
archive.objectLockUnknown: The archive is kept in the installation's default repository. Whether it has Object Lock is shown under Repositories.
archive.edition: Capture through Exchange journaling is part of the Business edition. Without it the setting is kept, but nothing is archived.

windows.applies: The limit that applies when a run starts is used for that whole run. A window that begins or ends during a run does not change it.
windows.rules: A window starts at its start time and ends just before its end time. An end that is not after the start ends on the next day; the same time twice makes a window of 24 hours. Windows must not overlap, but one can start where another ends.

mode.title: How to copy

overwrite.label: Overwrite
overwrite.description: Files of the source replace those with the same name. Nothing else in the target folder is touched.

mirror.label: Mirror
mirror.description: The target folder becomes the same as the source: what the source does not have is deleted.

mode.mirrorWarning: A mirror deletes files in the target folder. It refuses to run when the newest restore point is empty or has fewer than half the files of the last copy.

anyway.description: The copy runs even if the newest restore point is empty or has fewer than half the files of the last copy. In a mirror, files the source no longer has are deleted from the target folder.
